input: Label and store all camping gear in the shed

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing exactly which gear counts as 'camping gear' (tents, sleeping bags, cooking gear, clothing, tools, etc.) determines how much work is involved and whether anything gets left out or misplaced.
The current state and size of the shed — whether it is empty, already partially organised, or cluttered — directly affects how much prep work is needed before storing anything.
Whether this is for one person or a whole family (including kids) affects how items should be grouped, labelled, and made accessible.
A budget limit determines whether the plan can include purchasing shelving, storage bins, label makers, or other organisational tools.
The labelling method (hand-written tags, a label maker, colour-coded bins, etc.) and storage format (shelves, hooks, boxes) shape the specific steps and materials needed.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — e.g. everything fits, items are findable in under a minute, gear is protected from moisture — sets the quality bar for the final result.
Whether the priority is speed (get it done fast), cost (spend as little as possible), or neatness (a showroom-tidy result) changes which trade-offs to make throughout the task.

gold.taskTitle: Label and store all camping gear in shed
gold.taskDescription: Organise, label, and store all camping equipment neatly inside the shed so it is easy to find and access in the future.

questions.title: Which gear types are included — tents, cooking, clothing, all?
questions.description: Clarify the exact categories of camping equipment that need to be labelled and stored, so nothing is accidentally excluded or included.

questions.title: What is the shed's current state — empty, cluttered, or partial?
questions.description: Understand the starting condition of the shed to determine how much clearing or reorganising is needed before storage begins.

questions.title: Who needs to access this gear — just you, or the whole family?
questions.description: Identify all the people who will use the stored gear, which affects how items are grouped, labelled, and placed at appropriate heights.

questions.title: Is there a budget for bins, shelving, or labelling supplies?
questions.description: Establish any spending limit so the plan can be scoped to use existing materials or factor in purchasing organisational tools.

questions.title: What labelling method do you want — tags, label maker, colour codes?
questions.description: Determine the preferred system for labelling so the right materials and steps can be planned from the start.

questions.title: What does success look like — everything fits, gear is quickly findable?
questions.description: Define the specific outcome that means the task is truly complete, such as locating any item within a set time or ensuring gear is protected from weather.

questions.title: Is the priority speed, low cost, or a very neat final result?
questions.description: Identify the main priority so the right trade-offs are made — for example, whether to spend time on a perfect system or just get things stored quickly.
